active_paradigms.idea: Direct nonlinear optimization over centers+radii jointly with SLSQP, replacing the LP-for-fixed-centers decomposition
active_paradigms.description: Reformulate the packing as a single direct nonlinear program: variables are all 52 centers and 26 radii (78 total). Objective: maximize sum of radii. Constraints (all smooth, exact): for each pair (i,j): (x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2 >= (r_i+r_j)^2; for each circle and each wall: x_i-r_i>=0, 1-x_i-r_i>=0, same for y. Feed the current best solution (which scores 2.585) as the feasible warm start, so SLSQP starts from a valid point and can only improve. Unlike the current LP-on-fixed-centers approach (which restricts radii given frozen centers), this jointly moves centers and grows radii, escaping the fundamental limitation that the LP optimum is only optimal for the given positions. Run SLSQP with tolerance ~1e-10 and multiple restarts from perturbed feasible points within the time budget, keeping the best valid result. This directly attacks the gap: the current method's centers are only locally optimal under greedy axis-aligned moves, while SLSQP follows the true gradient of the joint problem.
active_paradigms.cautions: The 1e-6 overlap tolerance must be respected — shrink radii by 1e-7 margin in the objective. SLSQP with 78 variables needs a feasible warm start; use the current best arrangement as the start. Keep iterations bounded (~200) to fit the timeout. Verify validity with the evaluator's exact checks before returning.

active_paradigms.idea: Voronoi/power-diagram (Laguerre) fixed-point iteration for simultaneous repositioning
active_paradigms.description: For fixed radii, the optimal center placement relates to the power diagram (Laguerre Voronoi): each circle should sit at the incenter-like point of its power cell clipped to the square. Use an iterative fixed-point scheme: given current radii, compute the clipped Voronoi/power diagram of the 26 sites (scipy.spatial.Voronoi, manually clipping cells against the four walls), move each center toward the point of its cell that maximizes its distance to cell boundaries (the Chebyshev center of the cell — computable via small LP per cell or via the cell's incenter), then recompute radii with the existing LP. This is a fundamentally different geometric dynamic than greedy coordinate descent: it moves all circles simultaneously to their geometrically natural positions, often converging in 10-30 iterations to configurations unreachable by axis-aligned single/pair moves. Initialize from the current best solution and from the top few layout candidates.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii via better global center placement; validity
active_paradigms.cautions: Clip the Voronoi diagram to the unit square (use the half-plane representation of Voronoi ridges intersected with walls). Guard against degenerate cells (empty cells, vertices at infinity) by falling back to the previous iterate. Convergence can oscillate — damp with step factor 0.5 and keep the best-sum iterate rather than the last. Always recompute final radii with the existing LP (compute_max_radii) to guarantee validity.

active_paradigms.idea: Known-structure template seeding: enumerate contact-graph topologies and solve radii by LP on the exact contact structure
active_paradigms.description: The current program only tries 4 hand-designed layout templates. Instead, systematically enumerate plausible contact-structure templates: choose which circles touch which walls (corner circles touch 2 walls, edge circles 1, interior 0) and an adjacency graph consistent with a hexagonal-ish or mixed pattern. For each template, parametrize centers by the radii themselves: a circle touching the left wall has x=r; touching left and bottom has x=r, y=r; touching circle j and wall w gives one equation. This yields a system where positions are functions of radii, and maximizing sum of radii subject to the remaining non-overlap constraints becomes a small LP or least-squares fixed point. Concretely: generate templates by taking the known-best n=25 and n=27 packings' structure (documented in literature: n=26 optimal packings often derive from perturbing adjacent-n optima), plus asymmetric variants of the current layouts with 6 rows (e.g., 4,5,4,5,4,4 staggered), and rows of unequal spacing. Evaluate each template's radii via the existing LP and keep the best before a light polish. The key insight: the optimal n=26 packing is likely structurally asymmetric with several wall-bound large circles, which none of the current 4 templates capture well.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii by finding a better structural basin than the 4 current templates
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep the total number of enumerated templates modest (a few hundred) so LP evaluation stays within the timeout. Some templates will produce degenerate LPs (infeasible contact patterns) — skip them gracefully. The final answer must still pass the evaluator's pairwise check with the 1e-6 tolerance; apply the small safety margin. Combine with the existing Powell polish only as a final single step on the best template result.
